scope: Selected high-quality painting and technical comparisons, mainly c.1260–1500. Not a universal ranking or full census.

works.title: Crucifix, Santa Croce
works.why: Monumental full-body Passion painting before the first Lirey exhibitions; examine rib cage, torso shading, limbs and loincloth.
works.limitation: A panel painting, not painted linen. The 1966 flood destroyed about 60% of its painted surface; losses must not be treated as the original artist’s technique.

works.title: Crucifix, Santa Maria Novella
works.size: Monumental complete figure; exact body height not measured here
works.why: A strong early comparison for monumental painted anatomy, modeled flesh and Passion wounds. The close-up makes the facial technique visible.
works.limitation: The church page proposes 1288–89; other catalogues commonly use around 1290–95, and the archive discusses a later proposal. Wood, not linen. Image dimensions and cross dimensions do not equal the figure’s height.

works.title: Lamentation, Scrovegni Chapel
works.size: Museum record: approximately 200 × 200 cm, entire scene
works.why: An early-fourteenth-century treatment of Christ’s dead body, surrounding faces, bodily weight and grief.
works.limitation: A multi-figure wall painting, not a life-size body print or cloth painting. Chapel dating: https://cappelladegliscrovegni.it/index.php/it/la-cappella-di-giotto

works.title: Hours of Jeanne d’Evreux: Betrayal of Christ / Annunciation
works.material: Grisaille, tempera and ink on vellum
works.why: A named French royal artist working before Lirey. Especially useful for close inspection of French grisaille faces, hands and sculptural modeling.
works.limitation: An exceptionally small manuscript, not linen or a life-size figure. Enlargement reveals workmanship but does not change original scale.

works.title: Lamentation over the Dead Christ / Pietà di San Remigio
works.material: Tempera on wood with gold ground
works.why: A close chronological and thematic comparison for a dead Christ on a shroud, with modeled torso, limbs, wounds and intimate faces.
works.limitation: Date disagreement is retained rather than silently resolved. Whole-panel height does not establish a life-size Christ. The Bologna Zeri catalogue dates it 1360–65.

details.label: Christ and surrounding faces, official detail

works.artist: Attributed to Jean d’Orléans / Master of the Parement
works.title: Parement de Narbonne
works.material: Gray wash on moiré silk, subsequently mounted/lined
works.why: A near-period French monochrome Passion textile. A much closer support/function comparison than an unrelated oil painting.
works.limitation: Silk, not linen; figures are smaller than life-size. After the conventional first Lirey exhibition. The museum records attribution alternatives. c. 1375 is conventional and is not printed as a production date in this short Louvre record.

works.title: Saint Mary Magdalen / reverse: Flagellation of Christ
works.why: A substantial surviving double-sided painted processional textile with a complete standing Christ, torso modeling and Passion subject.
works.limitation: After both the conventional first Lirey display and the upper end of the 1988 interval. The Met calls the support canvas; this record does not independently establish its fiber as linen. Christ’s face on the reverse is a photographic facsimile of a detached medieval original, not original paint currently on the banner.

works.title: Four Passion scenes, Withyham / Leeds Castle group
works.material: Paint on linen with calcium-sulfate ground and animal glue; egg tempera reported
works.size: Each approximately 1 m²; exact figure heights not recovered
works.why: A genuinely near-period linen-painting group with specialist technical examination by Caroline Villers, John Stevenson and Jennifer Sharp. Flagellation and Mocking examined closely.
works.limitation: Original paper and notes are saved in the existing local library. No independently verified public image endpoint was recovered in this pass; this entry is a technical reference rather than an illustrated comparison. Around 1400 is later than first Lirey.

works.title: The Entombment
works.why: An especially useful later linen comparison: Christ’s body and burial shroud, faces and fine modeling, with a conservation literature describing actual painting materials.
works.limitation: Approximately a century after first Lirey; a small picture, not a life-size body. A published paint technique is not a Shroud-image mechanism.

details.label: National Gallery technical study: Bomford, Roy and Smith

works.title: The Annunciation
works.why: A second independently housed linen painting associated with the Bouts group, useful for fine facial modeling and understanding later cloth-painting practice.
works.limitation: A later comparison, not proof of what could be made in 1300s France. Not a Passion scene itself.

details.label: Getty catalogue with dimensions and medium

works.artist: Joos van Wassenhove / Justus of Ghent
works.title: The Adoration of the Magi
works.material: Distemper on canvas; technical study identifies linen
works.why: A major surviving cloth painting with fine faces, spatial composition and unusually helpful technical photographs and examination.
works.limitation: Later than first Lirey by over a century. Thin paint and exposed weave must not be equated with measured coloration inside Shroud fiber walls.

details.label: Met conservation researcher Sophie Scully and art historian Christine Seidel: full technical article

works.title: Lamentation over the Dead Christ
works.why: A later Renaissance comparison for an injured, foreshortened dead Christ on a burial surface; important for the “centuries ahead” visual comparison.
works.limitation: Around 130 years after first Lirey, not contemporaneous. The work is smaller than life-size and uses deliberate pictorial projection; realistic appearance is not a calibrated anatomical error measurement.
